solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After tan, ultimately, a holidaymaker removing nothing? Hardly!

definitions.text: After tan, ultimately, a holidaymaker removing nothing? Hardly!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the preceding word is kept
removing tells us to take a letter out of the word for a holidaymaker

blocks.note: the final letter of tan
taken as written
a holidaymaker is a tourist
nothing is zero, the letter O, which is taken out

explanation.surface: A sunbathing holidaymaker seems to be keeping all their clothes on, then the clue exclaims that this is hardly so.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a holidaymaker who removes nothing? Hardly, since this one removes everything, tan lines and all.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist on holiday strips off entirely, the very opposite of someone who removes no clothing.

clue.text: Woodcutter's excuse for cutting a beam oddly

indicators.note: cutting means the word for an excuse is trimmed, losing its final letter
oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the word before it

blocks.note: an alibi is an excuse; it loses its last letter
taken as written
the first and third letters of beam

explanation.surface: A woodcutter explains away some oddly cut timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('s = has, meaning the wordplay leads to it). In the Arabian Nights tale, the hero who finds the forty thieves' cave is a poor woodcutter.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of the Arabian Nights story of the forty thieves earns his living chopping wood.

clue.text: With little hope of one descending on concert, yours truly performs!

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming down on something means sitting directly above it, so this piece goes first

blocks.note: 'un is dialect for one, as in young 'un
a prom is a promenade concert
the setter referring to themselves
to sing is to perform

explanation.surface: A gloomy performer, about to step onto a concert stage, doubts how the show will go.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'descending on' places the first piece on top of the next. 'Un' for one is the dialect form heard in young 'un.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpromising shows few signs of future success, so it offers little hope.

clue.text: Bungling but penitent revolutionary guards

indicators.note: the words guard, or hold within them, a run of consecutive letters
something revolutionary turns over, so the held letters are read back to front

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of but and the start of penitent

explanation.surface: A clumsy but remorseful rebel stands guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept describes someone lacking skill, which is what bungling conveys.

clue.text: Initially troops in disarray used to shelter from attack

indicators.note: initially asks for just the opening letter of the next word
in disarray means thrown into confusion, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of troops
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a muddle fall back on their usual cover against an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints routed troops; the definition is the Roman formation in which soldiers locked shields overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A testudo was the Roman tortoise formation of overlapping shields protecting soldiers from missiles.

clue.text: In battalion's first reserve, I would add muscle

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word battalion

blocks.note: the opening letter of battalion
reserve in the sense of cool aloofness, ice
a postscript is what a letter-writer adds at the end

explanation.surface: An officer suggests strengthening the reserve unit of a battalion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like military reinforcements, but it means coolness of manner. PS is the postscript tag added below a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm.

clue.text: Old Belloc novel, one of many in circulation

indicators.note: novel means new or unusual, so the letters are given a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old novel by Hilaire Belloc is one of many copies still being passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In circulation' suggests books in print or on loan; here it is the circulation of the blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood cells are carried in vast numbers around the body by the circulatory system.

clue.text: Cold welcome for the true origin of Xmas

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hi is a word of greeting

explanation.surface: Christmas gets a frosty reception from purists who object to the abbreviation Xmas.
explanation.walkthrough: The X in Xmas is not a crossing-out but the Greek letter that begins the Greek name of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Xmas is formed from the Greek letter that opens Christos, so that letter is where the X really comes from.

clue.text: Model's rapid delivery: by November

blocks.note: patter is fast, glib talk
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fashion model speaks quickly, or a courier promises delivery by November.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a template or example to be copied, as a model is.

clue.text: Artist whose career is taking off?

blocks.note: first meaning: a painter of the school of Monet and Renoir
second meaning: an entertainer who mimics people, taking them off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' looks like a career that is soaring; it is the British sense of imitating someone for comic effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a member of a French painting movement and a performer who does impersonations of famous people.

clue.text: Act as solicitor, stopping first to visit restaurant?

indicators.note: stopping the first means halting the opening letter, so it is dropped

blocks.note: to act as something is to be a
a tout solicits custom or tickets

explanation.surface: A lawyer stops work first to go out for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it is someone touting for business. The phrase BE A TOUT loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat out is to have a meal away from home, typically at a restaurant.

clue.text: Still bright, short pants, maybe worn by maidens by day

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word for pants drops its last letter
a garment worn by people is around them, so this goes outside the next piece

blocks.note: pants in the British sense, underwear; the S is lost
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring, doubled for the plural
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Young women in short trousers, worn during the day, still look bright.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants are underpants. In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: Undimmed means not having lost brightness, so it is still shining as before.

clue.text: Note creature in river, brightly coloured: it advances from bank

blocks.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
a crocodile, short form, lives in rivers
red is a bright colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A colourful crocodile emerges from the water onto the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the river's edge from the surface; it is a lender making small loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Microcredit is the system of very small loans made to poor borrowers, typically by specialist banks.

clue.text: One's deified, having died in China in ancient city

indicators.note: in places the single letter for died inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a pal
taken as written
d is the abbreviation for died
Rome is the great city of antiquity

explanation.surface: A figure deified after dying in China, in the ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' places the letter, the second is taken as written. 'Deified' looks like making a god; it is a word that reads the same both ways, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word deified spells the same backwards and forwards, making it an example of such a word.

clue.text: Move quickly to get on panel

blocks.note: to dash is to move quickly
to board is to get on a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to catch a train, or to join a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashboard is the instrument panel in front of a driver.

clue.text: Inclined not to lose heart, if not exactly upfront

definitions.note: past participle; the answer is the verb or the adjective meaning slanting

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the word is removed
upfront says the approximate abbreviation is placed at the front

blocks.note: ca is circa, approximately
taken as written, then its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone tends not to get discouraged, even if they are not entirely straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not exactly upfront' sounds like evasive behaviour; split, it means circa placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant means to tilt or slope, so a canted surface is one set at a slant.

clue.text: One shown around foodstore

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
shown the way, guided

explanation.surface: A customer is given a tour of a food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods and fine ingredients.

clue.text: As strong gust changing direction, head for yacht

indicators.note: changing direction swaps one compass point for another in the word for a gust
head for means the leading letter of the next word

blocks.note: a squall is a sudden violent wind; its S (south) becomes E (east)
the opening letter of yacht

explanation.surface: A sailor notes that a gust has veered round as it heads for a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a mere joining word, but it is the definition: as tall as means equally tall.
explanation.definitionFit: In comparisons, as means to the same degree, which is what equally expresses.

clue.text: Period before spring was enthralling

definitions.note: the answer is the past tense of spellbind

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: A stretch of time just before springtime was captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' suggests the season; it is the verb meaning to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To spellbind is to enthral, so its past tense means held spectators enthralled.

clue.text: What could make me a lord?

definitions.text: What could make me a lord?

indicators.note: what could make asks what these letters might be made into once reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what honour would raise them to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: being granted this title would indeed make you a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving an earldom makes the holder an earl, a member of the British peerage addressed as Lord.

clue.text: Relatives of writer turned up with hacks

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to hack at something is to hew it

explanation.surface: A writer's relatives arrive along with some journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' suggests journalists, but it is the verb meaning chops.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephews are a sibling's sons, and so family relatives.

clue.text: In 1's pub, maybe good grill for the motorist

indicators.note: in places the letter for good inside the venue named next

blocks.note: a bar for naturists, the answer to 1 across
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: At a naturists' pub, a decent grilled meal is offered to drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grill' suggests food; here it is a metal frame. A nudge bar, also called a bull bar, is fitted to the front of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge bar is a protective metal grille fitted across the front of a car or truck.

clue.text: Sweet drink to have in your youth, primarily

indicators.note: to have something in is to hold it, so the drink goes around the next piece
primarily asks for the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
yr is the abbreviated form of your
the opening letter of youth

explanation.surface: A sweet drink is something to enjoy when you are young.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrupy means thick and sugary like syrup, so very sweet.

clue.text: Some yarn in English used in film

indicators.note: used in means put to work inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a skin is a thin film, as on custard
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A story told in English is used in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' and 'film' both suggest storytelling; one is wool, the other a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is a loosely coiled length of yarn or thread.

clue.text: Picture, evidential, led to disorder

indicators.note: led to disorder means brought into a jumbled state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A photograph used as evidence caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' suggests a photograph, but it means a film: the 1973 James Bond movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Live and Let Die is a James Bond film, and picture is a common word for a movie.

clue.text: Useless when one's no longer in front

indicators.note: no longer in means the single letter has gone from the word

blocks.note: a vain effort is a useless one
I is the Roman numeral for one, which is removed

explanation.surface: Someone feels useless once no longer at the forefront.
explanation.definitionFit: The van is the leading part of an army or movement, short for vanguard.

clue.text: Celebrated study, The Writer's Husband, recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole sequence is read in reverse

blocks.note: a den is a private study
the writer's means belonging to the setter, so my
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A well-known study titled The Writer's Husband is remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: To hymn something is to praise it in song, so hymned means celebrated.

clue.text: Notes time is extremely short?

blocks.note: minutes are written notes of a meeting
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Taking the minutes of a meeting leaves very little time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that short here means small in size rather than brief in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutest is the superlative of minute, meaning tiny, so it describes something extremely small.
